# PR #4031: Patch: the AI's count of the damage that gets past its Taunts lets a big attacker break a Taunt first, and keeps the attackers a Taunt's Armor would stop

Closes #3937

## What changed

The AI estimates how much damage the opponent can deal its hero next turn (`face_threat`, through `damage_past_taunts_with`). It now sends the opponent's attackers at its Taunts in the order a sensible opponent would. Before, it went smallest first and dropped any attacker a Taunt stopped whole. On the issue's board (a 3-health Defense guard with Armor 1, against attackers of 3, 3 and 4) it now counts 6 instead of 4. At 6 life, `wall_switches` now offers switching the second unit to Defense.

- **`crates/ai/src/config.rs`**: a new flag, `EvalWeights.best_attack_order_past_taunts`. It is on in `AI_EVAL` and off in `GREEDY_EVAL`, so the greedy baseline keeps the old count.
- **`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`**: the old walk moved into `soak_past_taunts`, which takes the order as an argument. With the flag on:
  - **Two orders:** the count is the larger of smallest first and "the smallest attacker that destroys this Taunt alone goes first". The second walk runs only when the first met a Taunt whose lone breaker had a smaller attacker ahead of it; otherwise the two walks are the same.
  - **Stopped attackers wait:** an attacker whose hit the Taunt's Armor takes whole, or that the Taunt's First Strike would destroy first, is kept instead of spent. When the Taunt falls it is free for the next Taunt or the hero.
  - **New helpers:** `dealt_after_armor` and `breaks_alone`.
  - With the flag off, the old walk runs unchanged.
- **Tests:**
  - **`position_model.rs`:** the `played` helper now plays every attack order and keeps the best. The Armor test now expects 2 (it was 0), and six new `r3937000_` tests cover the issue's board (6), a Taunt no attacker breaks alone, the two-orders case, a First Strike Taunt, attackers that may not hit the hero, and the flag's values in both weight sets.
  - **`search.rs`:** a new `wall_switches` test on the issue's board.
  - **`static_attack_flags.rs`:** the test's `OFF` weights also turn the new flag off.
  - **`lethal.rs`:** one pin moves from 0 to 3.
- **Docs:** a new ruling note `spec/rulings/R3937000.md`, its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/3937.md`, a link in the §9.9 Evaluation bullet, and a sentence in `crates/ai/README.md`.

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`: 46, 905 and 103 tests passed (7 ignored, the daily ones).
- **Each new test fails without the change.** I forced the flag off inside the walk and ran `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai -- r3937000`. The Armor, lone-breaker, First Strike and wall tests failed; the three tests that guard the old behaviour passed.
- **The two-orders rule is pinned.** With the walk changed to "breaker first only", the two-orders test and the may-not-hit-the-hero test both failed.
- The existing Poisonous, Trample, First Strike, Reborn, Divine Shield and Cleave tests pass unchanged, and no greedy test changed.
- `cargo jackioh gate` passed: ai-vs-random 20/20 (17 needed), ai-vs-greedy 17/20 (10 needed), hard-vs-easy 20/20 (16 needed), 0 search panics, and the perf and pinned checks passed.
- `cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts`:
  - The ai, cards, engine and run crates all passed.
  - In `jackioh-server`, `actor::duos::two_v_two::r3731002_four_sockets_play_a_two_v_two_to_its_end` failed once ("it is not your turn" for `a-end-1`). That run shared the CPU with the gate.
  - The test then passed 3 of 3 runs alone. A rerun of server, shared, tools and the wasm crates with `--no-fail-fast` was all green (server: 1,762 passed).
  - Four people hold that game's seats and the test asserts the AI played none of team B's turns, so I read the failure as timing under load, not this change. I have no link to it failing on `main`, so this is my reading, not a proof.
- `apps/web/src/wire` is unchanged after the workspace run.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **The larger of two orders, not the lone breaker alone.** The issue proposed sending the lone breaker first as the only order. On a full-health Defense guard (4 health, Armor 1) against four 2s and a 9, that counts 8. The opponent can deal 9: the 2s break the guard and the 9 goes face. A test pins this.

- **A Cleave attacker stopped by Armor waits, with no splash.** Before, its splash landed even though its hit did nothing. - **The `lethal.rs` pin moves from 0 to 3.** Prem Panther's 5 destroys Tommy Tempo (a 4/4 Taunt) alone, and Tempo Timmy's 3 then goes face. That is a line the opponent can actually play next turn.
- **One existing Cleave comment is now partly stale.** In `soak_past_taunts` it says the splash "lands even when the hit on the Taunt itself is stopped below". With the flag on, a hit the Armor would stop now waits before reaching that code; the new R3937000 comment just above says so.

# #3937: Patch: the AI's count of the damage that gets past its Taunts lets a big attacker break a Taunt first, and keeps the attackers a Taunt's Armor would stop
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Before it ends its turn, the practice AI counts how much damage the opponent's board could deal its hero next turn, so that it can see a lethal coming and switch a unit to Defense Position to block it. That count always sends the opponent's smallest attackers at the AI's guards first, and an attacker that would do nothing to a guard is dropped from the count instead of being kept for the hero. So the AI counts less than a sensible opponent would deal. Example: the AI is at 6 life with one unit guarding in Defense Position at 3 health, and the opponent has units with 3, 3 and 4 attack. The count sends the two 3s into the guard and only the 4 at the hero, 4 damage, so the AI feels safe and leaves its other unit in Attack Position. The opponent sends the 4 into the guard and both 3s at the hero: 6 damage, and the AI is dead. Once this is built, the count lets an attacker that can break a guard alone do it first and keeps the rest for the hero, so the AI sees that lethal and puts up a second guard.

## Why

- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:1164-1170`: `damage_past_taunts` sorts the free attackers smallest first (`free.sort_by_key(|(_, attack, may_hit_hero)| (*may_hit_hero, *attack))`) and spends them on the Taunts in that order.
- `evaluate.rs:1193-1195` and `:1271-1273`: an attacker that would fall to a First Strike Taunt, or whose hit the Taunt's Armor takes whole (`if dealt <= 0 { continue; }`), is used up from the bound list and never put back. Only the attackers never reached return to the free list (`:1282`).
- §4.2 step 3 only requires that a standing Taunt be the target (`crates/engine/src/combat.rs:546-560`); the attacking player picks the order. The function's own doc says it counts what the board could deal.
- A test pins the undercount: `crates/ai/tests/ai/position_model.rs:396-411` asserts 0 for two 1/4s and a 4/4 against a Defense Mr. Vanilla at 1 health with Armor 1, where the 4/4 sent first destroys it and the two 1s then deal 2. Its `played` helper (`:363-386`) also attacks smallest first.
- The number decides whether the AI looks for a blocking switch at all: `wall_switches` returns nothing while `face_threat` stays below the AI's life (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:961-966`, R2976000). It also feeds the evaluation's lethal threat and `ready_gap` (`crates/ai/src/lethal.rs:203`), which the opponent model's lethal reads.

## Proposal

- Keep an attacker that a Taunt would stop whole (Armor, or a First Strike that kills it) for the next Taunt or the hero, instead of discarding it.
- Before spending small attackers on a Taunt, send the smallest attacker that destroys it alone, when there is one; otherwise go smallest first as now.
- Keep it one cheap greedy pass, with no search.
- To keep the frozen greedy baseline still, put the new order behind an evaluation-weights flag, on in the AI's weights and off in the greedy's, as `gauntlet_bars_face_attacks` is (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:366,567,843`).
- Correct the pinned test to 2 and its `played` helper to play the best order.
- Update the AI README's sentence on the threat, and add a ruling in the issue's block if the bot finds §9.9 silent.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs` (`damage_past_taunts`), `crates/ai/src/config.rs`
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/position_model.rs`, a `wall_switches` test beside the R2976000 ones
- SPEC §9.9 and `crates/ai/README.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Armor test above expects 2, and a board with a 3-health Defense guard against 3, 3 and 4 attackers counts 6; both fail today.
- [ ] On that board with the AI at 6 life and a second unit in Attack Position, `wall_switches` offers switching it to Defense.
- [ ] A Taunt no single attacker can destroy is still soaked smallest first, and Reborn, Divine Shield, Trample and Poisonous keep their existing tests.
- [ ] The greedy baseline's weights leave the old order on, and its tests are unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` and `cargo jackioh gate` pass.

## Size and risks

Small to medium: one function, a flag, tests and a README line. Difficulty hard (the AI). Medium risk: the threat feeds every evaluation and one learned-evaluation input, so pinned AI fixtures and gate games may move. The gate shows whether it plays better or only differently.
